passages.text: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him, as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out, Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled from one town to another.
He went from village to village.
He preached the good news of the kingdom of God.
The Twelve disciples were with Jesus.
Some women were also with Him.
These women had been healed by Jesus.
He healed them from evil spirits and sicknesses.
One woman was Mary Magdalene.
Jesus had cast seven demons out of Mary Magdalene.
Another woman was Joanna.
Joanna was the wife of Chuza.
Chuza managed the household of Herod.
Another woman was Susanna.
Many other women were also there.
These women helped Jesus and His disciples.
They gave support from their own possessions.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς καὶ αὐτὸς διώδευεν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ κώμην κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οἱ δώδεκα σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες αἳ ἦσαν τεθεραπευμέναι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ ἀσθενειῶν Μαρία ἡ καλουμένη Μαγδαληνή ἀφ’ ἧς δαιμόνια ἑπτὰ ἐξεληλύθει καὶ Ἰωάννα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς

passages.text: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a large crowd gathering.
People were coming to Him from many towns.
Jesus spoke to them using a parable.
He said, “A farmer went out to sow his seed.
As the farmer scattered the seed, some seed fell along the path.
People trampled that seed.
Birds from the sky ate the seed.”
passages.original: Συνιόντος δὲ ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ἐπιπορευομένων πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν διὰ παραβολῆς Ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι τὸν σπόρον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν καὶ κατεπατήθη καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατέφαγεν αὐτό

passages.text: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable to a large crowd.
He said a farmer went out to sow his seed.
Some seed fell on rocky ground.
The seed grew up.
The seedlings withered.
They withered because they had no moisture.
passages.original: Καὶ ἕτερον κατέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν καὶ φυὲν ἐξηράνθη διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἰκμάδα

passages.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable to a large crowd.
He spoke about a farmer who sowed seed.
Some seed fell among thorns.
The thorns grew up with the seed.
The thorns choked the seed.
passages.original: Καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀκανθῶν καὶ συμφυεῖσαι αἱ ἄκανθαι ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτό

passages.text: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.” As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable about the word of God.
The seed in the parable means the word of God.
Some seed fell on good soil.
The seed grew in the good soil.
It produced a crop.
The crop was a hundred times more than what was sown.
As Jesus spoke these words, He called out loudly.
Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν καὶ φυὲν ἐποίησεν καρπὸν ἑκατονταπλασίονα Ταῦτα λέγων ἐφώνει Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω

passages.text: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught His disciples.
His disciples listened to Jesus.
His disciples did not understand the parable.
His disciples asked Jesus a question.
They asked, “What does this parable mean?”
passages.original: Ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ Τίς αὕτη εἴη ἡ παραβολή

passages.text: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that, ‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “God has given you the knowledge of the mysteries of His kingdom.
God has not given this knowledge to others.
I speak to others using parables.
They see, but they do not truly see.
They hear, but they do not understand.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἵνα Βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσιν Καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ συνιῶσιν

passages.text: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He explained the parable to them.
The parable has a meaning.
The seed in the parable is the word of God.
passages.original: Ἔστιν δὲ αὕτη ἡ παραβολή ὁ σπόρος ἐστὶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
passages.sermon:
Jesus explained the meaning of the parable.
The seed represents the word of God.
The seeds along the path are people who hear the word.
The devil comes to these people.
The devil takes the word away from their hearts.
These people do not believe.
These people are not saved.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες εἶτα ἔρχεται ὁ διάβολος καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ πιστεύσαντες σωθῶσιν

passages.text: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
passages.sermon:
The seeds on rocky ground are people.
These people hear the word of God.
They receive the word with joy.
They do not have a root.
They believe for a short time.
When testing comes, they fall away.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς πέτρας οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν μετὰ χαρᾶς δέχονται τὸν λόγον καὶ οὗτοι ῥίζαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν οἳ πρὸς καιρὸν πιστεύουσιν καὶ ἐν καιρῷ πειρασμοῦ ἀφίστανται

passages.text: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
passages.sermon:
Some people are like seeds that fall among thorns.
These people hear the word.
As they go through life, worries choke them.
Riches also choke them.
Pleasures of this life choke them too.
Because of this, their fruit does not mature.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας πεσόν οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες καὶ ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν καὶ πλούτου καὶ ἡδονῶν τοῦ βίου πορευόμενοι συμπνίγονται καὶ οὐ τελεσφοροῦσιν

passages.text: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.
passages.sermon:
The seeds on good soil are people with a noble and good heart.
They hear the word.
They hold on to the word.
They keep the word firmly.
They persevere.
They produce a crop.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ ἐν τῇ καλῇ γῇ οὗτοί εἰσιν οἵτινες ἐν καρδίᾳ καλῇ καὶ ἀγαθῇ ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον κατέχουσιν καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν ὑπομονῇ

passages.text: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
passages.sermon:
A person lights a lamp.
He does not cover the lamp with a jar.
He does not put the lamp under a bed.
He puts the lamp on a stand.
People enter the room.
They see the light from the lamp.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς δὲ λύχνον ἅψας καλύπτει αὐτὸν σκεύει ἢ ὑποκάτω κλίνης τίθησιν ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ λυχνίας τίθησιν ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς

passages.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
passages.sermon:
Nothing hidden will stay hidden.
Everything hidden will be revealed.
Nothing concealed will remain secret.
Everything concealed will be made known.
Everything concealed will come into the open.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ φανερὸν γενήσεται οὐδὲ ἀπόκρυφον ὃ οὐ μὴ γνωσθῇ καὶ εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ

passages.text: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them to pay close attention to how they listen.
He said, “Whoever has will receive more.
Whoever does not have will lose even what he thinks he has.”
passages.original: Βλέπετε οὖν πῶς ἀκούετε ὃς ἂν γὰρ ἔχῃ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ἔχῃ καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had a mother.
Jesus had brothers.
His mother and brothers came to see Him.
A large crowd surrounded Jesus.
The crowd blocked the way.
His mother and brothers could not reach Him.
passages.original: Παρεγένετο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο συντυχεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον

passages.text: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was inside a house.
A crowd surrounded Him.
Someone spoke to Jesus.
The person said, “Your mother is outside.”
The person also said, “Your brothers are outside.”
They are standing outside.
They want to see You.
passages.original: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ αὐτῷ Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν θέλοντές σε

passages.text: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He answered them.
He said, “My mother and my brothers are here.
They are the ones who hear the word of God.
They also do what God says.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες

passages.text: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was a teacher and leader.
He had disciples who followed Him.
One day, Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.”
Jesus got into a boat.
His disciples got into the boat with Him.
They set out together across the lake.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης καὶ ἀνήχθησαν

passages.text: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples sailed on the lake.
Jesus fell asleep.
A strong windstorm came down on the lake.
The boat began to fill with water.
They were in great danger.
passages.original: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον

passages.text: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the boat with His disciples.
A strong windstorm struck the lake.
The boat began to fill with water.
The disciples were afraid.
The disciples went to Jesus.
They woke Him up.
They said, “Master, Master, we are perishing!”
Jesus got up.
He spoke to the wind.
He spoke to the raging waters.
The wind stopped.
The waters became calm.
There was complete peace.
passages.original: Προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα ἀπολλύμεθα Ὁ δὲ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος καὶ ἐπαύσαντο καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη

passages.text: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Where is your faith?”
The disciples felt afraid.
They were also amazed.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Who is this?”
They said, “He commands even the winds and the water.”
They said, “The winds and the water obey Him.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ποῦ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν Φοβηθέντες δὲ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ἐπιτάσσει καὶ τῷ ὕδατι καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
passages.sermon: Jesus and His disciples sailed in a boat.\r\nThey traveled across the lake from Galilee.\r\nThey arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
passages.original: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας

passages.text: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stepped ashore.
A man met Jesus.
This man came from the town.
This man was possessed by demons.
For a long time, the man had not worn clothes.
He did not live in a house.
He stayed among the tombs.
passages.original: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἔχων δαιμόνια καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλ’ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν

passages.text: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”
passages.sermon:
A man lived in the region of the Gerasenes.
This man was possessed by many demons.
He did not wear clothes.
He did not live in a house.
He stayed among the tombs.
Jesus stepped onto the shore.
The demon-possessed man saw Jesus.
He cried out loudly.
He fell down before Jesus.
He shouted with a loud voice.
He said, “What do you want with me, Jesus?”
He said, “You are the Son of the Most High God.”
He begged Jesus.
He said, “Do not torture me!”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί Ἰησοῦ Υἱὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου δέομαί σου μή με βασανίσῃς

passages.text: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a man who was possessed by an unclean spirit.
Jesus commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man.
The unclean spirit had controlled the man for a long time.
People had often bound the man with chains and shackles.
The man broke the chains many times.
The demon drove the man into lonely and deserted places.
passages.original: παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν καὶ ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος καὶ διαρρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους

passages.text: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus asked the man a question.
Jesus said, “What is your name?”
The man answered Jesus.
The man said, “Legion.”
Many demons had entered the man.
The man had many demons inside him.
That is why he said his name was Legion.
passages.original: Ἐπηρώτησεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τί σοι ὄνομά ἐστιν ὁ Δὲ εἶπεν Λεγιών ὅτι εἰσῆλθεν δαιμόνια πολλὰ εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.
passages.sermon:
Jesus met a man who was possessed by many demons.
These demons had entered the man and controlled him for a long time.
The demons spoke to Jesus.
The demons begged Jesus.
They asked Jesus not to command them to go into the Abyss.
The Abyss is a place of punishment for evil spirits.
The demons did not want to be sent there.
passages.original: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μὴ ἐπιτάξῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἀπελθεῖν

passages.text: There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.
passages.sermon:
A large herd of pigs was on the hillside.
The pigs were feeding there.
Many demons were present.
The demons spoke to Jesus.
The demons begged Jesus for permission.
They asked Jesus to let them enter the pigs.
Jesus gave the demons permission to enter the pigs.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἀγέλη χοίρων ἱκανῶν βοσκομένη ἐν τῷ ὄρει καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιτρέψῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς ἐκείνους εἰσελθεῖν καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
passages.sermon:
Jesus met a man who had demons inside him.
The demons left the man.
The demons entered the pigs.
A large herd of pigs was on the hillside.
The pigs rushed down the steep bank.
The pigs ran into the lake.
The pigs drowned in the water.
passages.original: Ἐξελθόντα δὲ τὰ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ ἀπεπνίγη

passages.text: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.
passages.sermon:
Some men were watching the pigs.
These men saw what happened.
They became afraid.
They ran away.
They went to the town.
They also went to the countryside.
They told people what had happened.
passages.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ βόσκοντες τὸ γεγονὸς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς

passages.text: So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
passages.sermon:
The people heard what happened.
They went out to see for themselves.
They came to Jesus.
They saw the man who had been possessed by demons.
The man sat at Jesus’ feet.
He wore clothes.
He was in his right mind.
The people became afraid.
passages.original: ἐξῆλθον δὲ ἰδεῖν τὸ γεγονὸς καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ εὗρον καθήμενον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφ’ οὗ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐξῆλθεν ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν

passages.text: Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
passages.sermon:
Some people saw what happened.
These people had witnessed the event.
They reported what they saw.
They explained how the demon-possessed man was healed.
passages.original: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐσώθη ὁ δαιμονισθείς

passages.text: Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had healed a man who was possessed by demons in the region of the Gerasenes.
All the people in that region saw what happened.
The people became very afraid.
The people asked Jesus to leave them.
Jesus got into a boat.
Jesus started to return.
passages.original: Καὶ ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου τῶν Γερασηνῶν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὅτι φόβῳ μεγάλῳ συνείχοντο αὐτὸς δὲ ἐμβὰς εἰς πλοῖον ὑπέστρεψεν

passages.text: The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying, “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had healed a man who was possessed by demons.
The man begged Jesus to let him go with Him.
Jesus did not let the man go with Him.
Jesus told the man to return home.
Jesus told the man to tell others what God had done for him.
The man went away.
The man told people throughout the whole town what Jesus had done for him.
passages.original: Ἐδεῖτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀφ’ οὗ ἐξεληλύθει τὰ δαιμόνια εἶναι σὺν αὐτῷ ἀπέλυσεν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγων Ὑπόστρεφε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου καὶ διηγοῦ ὅσα σοι ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καθ’ ὅλην τὴν πόλιν κηρύσσων ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus returned.\r\nThe crowd welcomed Him.\r\nAll the people had been waiting for Him.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑποστρέφειν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπεδέξατο αὐτὸν ὁ ὄχλος ἦσαν γὰρ πάντες προσδοκῶντες αὐτόν

passages.text: Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus’ feet. He begged Him to come to his house, because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying. As Jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around Him, including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.
passages.sermon:
Jairus was a synagogue leader.
Jairus came to Jesus.
Jairus fell at Jesus’ feet.
Jairus begged Jesus to come to his house.
Jairus had one daughter.
His daughter was about twelve years old.
His daughter was dying.
Jesus went with Jairus.
Crowds pressed around Jesus as He went.
A woman was in the crowd.
This woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She had spent all her money on doctors.
No one was able to heal her.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν ἀνὴρ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰάϊρος καὶ οὗτος ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς ὑπῆρχεν καὶ πεσὼν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα ἥτις ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἀπ’ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι

passages.text: She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
passages.sermon:
A woman had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She came up behind Jesus.
She touched the edge of His cloak.
Her bleeding stopped at once.
passages.original: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς

passages.text: “Who touched Me?” Jesus asked. But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke.
He asked, “Who touched Me?”
Everyone denied touching Him.
Peter answered Jesus.
Peter called Jesus “Master.”
Peter said, “The people are crowding You.”
Peter said, “The people are pressing against You.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τίς ὁ ἁψάμενός μου Ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος Ἐπιστάτα οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ἀποθλίβουσιν

passages.text: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke.\r\nHe said, “Someone touched Me.”\r\nJesus knew this because power had gone out from Him.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἥψατό μού τις ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
passages.sermon:
A woman had touched Jesus.
She realized she could not hide.
She began to tremble.
She came to Jesus.
She fell down before Him.
All the people were watching.
She explained why she had touched Jesus.
She said she had been healed immediately.
passages.original: Ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα

passages.text: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He called her "Daughter."
He said her faith had healed her.
He told her to go in peace.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Θυγάτηρ ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην

passages.text: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was still speaking.
A man came from the house of the synagogue leader.
The synagogue leader was named Jairus.
The man spoke to Jairus.
He said, “Your daughter is dead.”
He said, “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”
passages.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν Διδάσκαλον

passages.text: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard the message.
He spoke to Jairus.
Jesus said, “Do not be afraid.”
He said, “Only believe.”
He said, “She will be healed.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Μὴ φοβοῦ μόνον πίστευσον καὶ σωθήσεται

passages.text: When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the house.
He did not allow anyone else to go in with Him.
He allowed only Peter to go in with Him.
He allowed only John to go in with Him.
He allowed only James to go in with Him.
He allowed the child’s father to go in with Him.
He allowed the child’s mother to go in with Him.
passages.original: Ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν τινα σὺν αὐτῷ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα

passages.text: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”
passages.sermon:
Everyone was weeping for the girl.
Everyone was mourning for her.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Stop weeping.”
Jesus said, “She is not dead.”
Jesus said, “She is asleep.”
passages.original: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Μὴ κλαίετε οὐ γὰρ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει

passages.text: And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.
passages.sermon: The people in the house knew the child was dead.\r\nThey laughed at Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present with the girl who had died.
Jesus took the girl’s hand.
Jesus spoke loudly.
Jesus said, “Child, get up!”
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων Ἡ Παῖς ἔγειρε

passages.text: Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood by the dead girl.
He took her by the hand.
Her spirit returned to her.
She got up at once.
Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν

passages.text: Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had just raised a dead girl to life.
Her parents saw this.
Her parents were amazed.
Jesus spoke to her parents.
Jesus told them not to tell anyone what had happened.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός
